questions.prompt: Put the journey of a request through an ASP.NET Core application in order.
steps: The client sends an HTTP request
Kestrel accepts the request and forwards it to the ASP.NET Core pipeline
Middleware processes the request and routing picks the controller action
The controller calls the business logic in the services
The data access layer (repository / EF Core) reads or updates the database
The response passes back through the middleware to the client
questions.explanation: Kestrel receives the request, the middleware pipeline and routing hand it to a controller, the controller works through services and data access, and the response returns through the pipeline.

questions.prompt: What is Kestrel's role in an ASP.NET Core app?
options: It is a reverse proxy that only runs on Windows in front of IIS
It is the ORM that maps controllers to database tables
It is the default cross-platform web server: it accepts HTTP requests and forwards them into the ASP.NET Core pipeline
It is the middleware that decides which controller handles a request
questions.explanation: Kestrel is ASP.NET Core's default web server. It handles the network communication and can run on its own or behind a reverse proxy such as IIS, Nginx or Apache.

questions.prompt: What can each middleware component in the pipeline do with a request?
options: Modify it, pass it to the next middleware, or stop the pipeline
Only read it; changes are made by the controller
Only pass it on; middleware cannot end a request early
Only run after the controller has produced a response
questions.explanation: Each middleware can process the request, decide to pass it to the next component, or terminate the pipeline, for example when a request is unauthorized.

questions.prompt: Why does a Web API controller derive from `ControllerBase` while an MVC controller derives from `Controller`?
options: `ControllerBase` is faster because it skips routing
`Controller` adds view (HTML) support, which an API that returns JSON does not need
questions.explanation: Web API returns data such as JSON with no view support, so it uses `ControllerBase`; MVC renders HTML views and uses `Controller`.

questions.prompt: Which project is the best fit for a Minimal API, according to the lesson?
options: A large enterprise ERP with dozens of controllers
A small weather-notification microservice with three endpoints
A server-rendered website built with Razor views
A real-time chat app that needs SignalR
questions.explanation: Minimal APIs are best for lightweight microservices and prototypes, such as a service with a few endpoints or a proof of concept where speed matters more than structure.
